messages.author: 2943e6ad5bf30f8c
messages.subject: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed
parts:
I've in my data, timestamps, traffic flow, sensorID, and Longitude & Latitude!
I'm trying to predict the traffic flow in each location using INLA but I keep getting error when I try to apply INLA

Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.


I'm new to INLA and want to use it in my research but not quit sure if I'm missing something in my code!

here's my code :
data$timestamp<- as.POSIXct(data$timestamp, tz="GMT", format = "%m/%d/%y %H:%M")
coords <- cbind( data$Longitude, data$Latitude)
plot(coords)
coords.sp <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(coords))
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(coords.sp, max.edge = c(20, 40))
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh, alpha = 2)
index = inla.spde.make.index("spatial", mesh$n)
A = inla.spde.make.A(mesh, coords.sp, index=1:n)
stack = inla.stack(data=list(count=data$Flow), A=list(A, 1), effects=list(c(index, list(intercept=1)), list(spray=data$ID)))

##And here where I get the error when I run the code!:
 data.inla <- inla(y ~ 0 + Intercept + f(spatial.field, model = spde), data = inla.stack.data(stack), control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack)))


Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

Anyone familiar with the error or suggest a solution?
Many thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed
parts:
Your code calls the observations "count" when constructing the stack, but "y" in the formula.

Finn
